2027-06-05.title: Saturday of the second week after Pentecost · St Boniface
readings: From childhood you have known the sacred writings; all scripture is inspired by God
“David himself calls him Lord; so how can he be his son?”
2027-06-05.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Second Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam remembers St Boniface, bishop and martyr, the apostle of the Germans (Panchangam 2026–27, p. 56). On this Saturday the Latin Church also honours the Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary. 5 June is World Environment Day.
2027-06-05.verse: All scripture is inspired by God and is useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness, so that everyone who belongs to God may be proficient, equipped for every good work.
theo: St Paul's second letter to Timothy is the letter of an old man in prison who knows that his end is near. He writes to his son in the faith not about himself but about what must be handed on. “Now you have observed my teaching, my conduct, my aim in life, my faith, my patience, my love, my steadfastness, my persecutions, and my suffering the things that happened to me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra.” Timothy had seen it all at close range. Paul does not hide the cost: “Indeed, all who want to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.” Then he points to the two things that will keep Timothy steady when he himself is gone: the people from whom he learned the faith, and the Scriptures he has known since he was a child. “But as for you, continue in what you have learned and firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it, and how from childhood you have known the sacred writings that are able to instruct you for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.” Timothy learned the Scriptures on the knees of his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice. Many of us learned them in the same way: a grandmother reading the Bible aloud in the evening by the oil lamp, a mother teaching the first prayers, a Sunday school teacher who made the stories come alive.

Then comes one of the great sentences about the Bible: “All scripture is inspired by God and is useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness, so that everyone who belongs to God may be proficient, equipped for every good work.” The word Paul uses means “God-breathed”. The same breath that gave life to Adam and that the risen Christ breathed on the apostles is in the words of Scripture. That is why the Church reads them in every Holy Qurbono, carries the Gospel book in procession, and kisses it. The Gospel today shows Jesus himself reading Scripture with authority. He quotes Psalm 110: “David himself, by the Holy Spirit, declared, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies under your feet.”’ David himself calls him Lord; so how can he be his son?” The Messiah is David's son by birth, and yet David calls him Lord: he is more than a king of David's line; he is the Son of God, seated at the Father's right hand. Mark adds: “And the large crowd was listening to him with delight.” The word of God, opened by Christ, is not a burden but a joy.

St Boniface, whom the Panchangam remembers today, lived this love of Scripture to the end. Born in Wessex in England about 675 and named Wynfrith, he became a monk and a teacher of the Bible, and he could have stayed in his monastery all his life. But he heard the call to bring the Gospel to the Germanic peoples. Pope Gregory II sent him in 719 and gave him the name Boniface. He preached, baptized, founded monasteries and dioceses, and became the archbishop of the German lands. In old age he went back once more to Frisia, the land where he had first tried to preach. On 5 June 754, at Dokkum, a band of armed men attacked him and his companions as they waited to confirm the newly baptized. Boniface told his companions not to fight. An ancient tradition says that he raised a book of the Gospels over his head as the sword came down. In a letter he once wrote that the Church is like a great ship tossed on the sea, and that the shepherd must not abandon it but keep it on its course (Letter to Cuthbert, in substance). On this Saturday the Latin Church also honours the Immaculate Heart of Mary, who “treasured all these things in her heart”. Like Timothy's mother and grandmother, like Boniface, the Mother of God teaches us to keep God's word in our hearts and to hand it on.
outline: Ask: from whom did I learn the faith, and to whom am I handing it on?
Point 1 · Continue in what you have learned
The people and the Scriptures that formed us from childhood.
The word that teaches, corrects and equips us for every good work.
Point 3 · David's son and David's Lord
Jesus opens the Scriptures; St Boniface died with the Gospel in his hands.
live: Continue in what you have learned (2 Timothy 3:14)
Thank God today by name for the person who first taught you to pray or read the Bible.
Equipped for every good work (2 Timothy 3:17)
Read one chapter of a Gospel today, slowly, and choose one good work it asks of you.
2027-06-05.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Son of David and Lord of David, seated at the right hand of the Father, you opened the Scriptures to the crowds, and they listened with delight. Give us that same delight in your word. Bless the grandparents, parents and teachers who hand on the faith to children, and keep us faithful to what we have learned. Through the prayers of St Boniface, who carried your Gospel to the nations and gave his life holding it, make us bold to proclaim your word in season and out of season. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono the Gospel book is carried with candles and incense, because in it Christ himself speaks. The God-breathed word prepares the way for the Word made flesh, who gives himself to us on the altar.
conn: 2 Timothy 3:15 says the Scriptures instruct us for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus; in Mark 12:35–37 Christ himself shows that Psalm 110 speaks of him.
The Latin Church keeps the Immaculate Heart of Mary on this Saturday, with the Gospel of Luke 2:41–51, where the Mother of God “treasured all these things in her heart”.
fathers: Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ (Commentary on Isaiah, Prologue).

The Church is like a great ship sailing on the sea of this world, struck by the waves of trials; we must not abandon it but steer it, not be silent watchers or hirelings who run from the wolf, but watchful shepherds (Letter to Cuthbert, in substance).
magis: Holy Mother Church holds that the books of both the Old and the New Testament, in their entirety, are sacred and canonical, because, written under the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, they have God as their author and teach firmly, faithfully and without error the truth which God wanted put into the sacred writings for the sake of our salvation.

The Church forcefully and specifically exhorts all the Christian faithful to learn the surpassing knowledge of Jesus Christ by frequent reading of the divine Scriptures, for ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ.

quick: Paul reminds Timothy of all he has seen and suffered, and tells him to continue in what he learned from childhood.
All scripture is inspired by God and useful for teaching, reproof, correction and training in righteousness.
Jesus asks how the Messiah can be David's son if David calls him Lord; St Boniface, apostle of the Germans, was martyred in 754.
2027-06-05.action: Read a chapter of the Bible today with a child or a grandparent.
2027-06-05.question: Do I come to the word of God with delight, or only out of habit?

family.explain: St Paul wrote to his young friend Timothy: remember the Bible stories you learned when you were a child. Timothy's grandmother Lois and mother Eunice had taught him. Paul says that every part of the Bible is breathed by God, like God breathing life into us. Long ago a monk called Boniface loved the Bible so much that he carried it to faraway lands, and when bad men attacked him, he held the Gospel book above his head.
family.intention: We pray for all grandparents, parents and teachers who teach children about God.
family.ask: Ask: “What is my favourite Bible story, and who first told it to me?”

illus: A woman from a parish in Kottayam district, now a doctor in a city in North India, still keeps the Bible her grandmother used. It is falling apart, the cover held together with tape, and the margins are full of dates written in pencil: the day a grandson was born, the day a son left for the Gulf, the day the old house flooded. Next to each date is a verse number. When the doctor was a child, her grandmother made her read a verse aloud every evening after the family prayer, and then asked her one question about it. She says she hated it at the time. Now, alone in a hospital flat at the end of long night shifts, she opens the book and reads the verses her grandmother chose for the hard days of her own life, and finds them still speaking.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, who breathed the Scriptures, open our hearts to the word of God and give us delight in it. Amen.
share: But as for you, continue in what you have learned and firmly believed, knowing from whom you learned it (2 Timothy 3:14). Who taught me the faith, and how can I honour them?
All scripture is inspired by God and is useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness (2 Timothy 3:16). When did a word of Scripture correct me?
And the large crowd was listening to him with delight (Mark 12:37). What word of Jesus brings me joy?
pm.resp: Lord, your word is a lamp to my feet.
interc: For the Church, that she may love and proclaim the word of God in season and out of season.
For grandparents, parents and catechists, that they may hand on the faith to children with patience and joy.
For missionaries who carry the Gospel to new peoples, that they may have the courage of St Boniface.
For all who suffer for the faith, that the word of God may be their strength.
For the care of creation on this World Environment Day, that we may be good stewards of the earth God has given us.
pm.close: Father, you breathed your word into the Scriptures and gave us your Son, the Lord of David. Through the prayers of St Boniface, give us delight in your word and courage to hand it on. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: From the Greek word in 2 Timothy 3:16, theopneustos, “God-breathed”. The Church teaches that God is the author of Sacred Scripture, and that he chose human writers who, using their own abilities, wrote everything and only what he wanted written, so that the Bible teaches without error the truth God wished to reveal for our salvation (Dei Verbum 11).
kidsaint: St Boniface and the great oak

St Boniface was a monk from England who went to teach the people of Germany about Jesus. Some of them were afraid of a huge old oak tree at Geismar that they believed was sacred to a pagan god. Boniface took an axe and cut it down, and nothing bad happened to him. The people saw that their old god had no power, and many became Christians. Boniface used the wood to build a little chapel. Many years later, when he was very old, he was killed by robbers while he waited to confirm new Christians. Lesson: do not be afraid; Jesus is stronger than anything that frightens us.

homily: Dear friends, today St Paul, old and in prison, writes to his young friend Timothy. He reminds him of everything he has seen and suffered, and he tells him: Indeed, all who want to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted (2 Timothy 3:12). But he also tells him where to find strength: in the people who taught him the faith, and in the Scriptures he has known from childhood.

Paul says: All scripture is inspired by God and is useful for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for training in righteousness (2 Timothy 3:16). The Bible is breathed by God. It teaches us, it corrects us, and it makes us ready for every good work. That is why we listen to it in every Holy Qurbono, and why we should read it at home.

In the Gospel Jesus reads the Psalms and shows that they speak of him: David himself calls him Lord; so how can he be his son? (Mark 12:37). Jesus is the Son of David, but also David's Lord, the Son of God. And the large crowd was listening to him with delight (Mark 12:37). God's word is meant to bring us joy.

Today we remember St Boniface, who carried the Gospel from England to the German peoples and died a martyr in 754, holding, so tradition says, a book of the Gospels. Let us thank God for those who taught us the faith, let us read the Bible with delight, and let us hand it on to our children. Amen.
kids: Children, who taught you your first prayers? Maybe your grandmother, or your mother, or your teacher at Sunday school. St Paul's friend Timothy learned about God from his grandmother and his mother. Paul says that the Bible is breathed by God, like when God breathed life into Adam. Today we remember St Boniface, who loved the Bible so much that he carried it to faraway countries. Ask someone at home to read you a Bible story tonight, and listen with joy!

intro: Theme: “All scripture is inspired by God.”
On Saturday of the second week after Pentecost, the memory of St Boniface: continuing in what we have learned, the God-breathed Scriptures, and Christ who is both David's son and David's Lord.

points.h: Continue in what you have learned
sub: Knowing from whom you learned it.
Lois, Eunice and our own grandmothers.
q: Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise.
I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and now, I am sure, lives in you.
points.apply: Set a fixed time this week for the family to read a passage of Scripture together, even for five minutes.

sub: For correction and training in righteousness.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
because no prophecy ever came by human will, but men and women moved by the Holy Spirit spoke from God.
points.apply: Keep a Bible or a Gospel book where you can see it at home, and open it once a day.

sub: More than a king: the Son at the right hand.
The crowd listened with delight; Boniface held the Gospel to the end.
q: The Lord says to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool.”
and every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
points.apply: When you hear the Gospel at the next Holy Qurbono, listen for one word that brings you joy, and carry it with you through the day.

concl: The Scriptures we learned as children are breathed by God, and they lead us to Christ, David's son and David's Lord.
St Boniface carried them to the nations and died holding them.
2027-06-05.resolve: Read the word of God with delight, continue in what you have learned, and hand it on.
